revisionDesc.change: Submit - Korrektur Z.14 A. Benaissa, P.Oxy. 87 5615.3 n.

Vote - AcceptText - At the end of lin5 after the clear ριν there is what is probably a dot of ink (not raised). The long upper portion of the sigma from ἀρούρας in the following line makes the reading less easy. It almost looks like a little thickening of the ink at the very outermost part of the diagonal of the sigma. I think that Ταυρίνο̣(υ)) is quite acceptable.

Vote - AcceptText - This looks very convincing to me. I have only a scan of the volume and thus I'm not sure I can see traces of the (I assume) superscript omicron at the end of line 5: could the next voter check, please? An abbreviation without raised omikrong wouldn't be absurd either. The form of the beta is a bit unusal, but not inconceivable, and the sense supports the reading. BL corrections checked and fine, regularization without correction is also fine.

Submit - Changed the ghost-name Ταυριννοηθου in l. 5-6 to Ταυρίνο(υ) / βοηθοῦ upon checking the Plate in the edition. Beta with an acceptable form, not unparalleled. This reading also affects line 1. In line 13, the name has been already corrected to a substantive by E. Wipszycka (see BL). Additionally, I have regularized the preceding article and pronoun (as this is quite obvious, I did not include my name in the correction).
